messages.content: Let’s settle the hotels for the Nashville and Raleigh circuit. The flights now mean Sunday arrival in Nashville, Wednesday around midday to Raleigh, and Saturday evening home. I need three nights in each city.

Understood: Nashville check-in Sunday, January 25 and checkout Wednesday, January 28; Raleigh check-in Wednesday, January 28 and checkout Saturday, January 31. I’ll compare the two lodging choices in each city on tax-inclusive cost, ground transportation, cancellation timing, and Saturday luggage handling.
For Nashville, the campus guest hotel quoted $189 a night before tax. The downtown hotel is $214. Can you put those on an equal basis?

Using the quoted rates for three nights and the applicable lodging taxes shown with each offer, the campus guest hotel comes to $656.40 including tax. The downtown hotel comes to $739.26 including tax. The downtown option is $82.86 more for the stay. Neither quote shows a resort or destination fee, but that should be reconfirmed before booking.
The Monday dinner is downtown, while Tuesday is entirely on campus. I’ll arrive at the airport around 6:15 Sunday evening. How does transportation change the comparison?

For the campus hotel, allow about $34 for a car from the airport, $16 each way for Monday’s downtown dinner, and no car for Tuesday if the meetings are walkable. That is roughly $66 in local cars. For the downtown hotel, estimate $26 from the airport, no car for Monday dinner if the address is walkable, and about $18 each way for Tuesday’s campus meetings, or roughly $62. The estimated transportation difference is negligible, so the campus option remains about $79 less overall.
That makes the campus hotel sound better. Is there any practical reason to pay more for downtown?

Downtown gives you the simpler first evening and Monday dinner logistics, especially if dinner runs late. The campus property avoids Tuesday commuting and costs less. Since Tuesday is the full workday and Monday requires only one round trip, the campus hotel is the more efficient choice unless the dinner address turns out to be far enough away to raise the car estimate materially.
What are the cancellation deadlines?

The campus quote is cancellable without penalty until 6:00 p.m. local time on Friday, January 23; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax. The downtown offer allows cancellation until 11:59 p.m. local time on Saturday, January 24, also with a one-night-plus-tax penalty afterward. The downtown hotel gives roughly one extra day of flexibility.
Choose the campus guest hotel. Please note a standard king, nonsmoking, and late arrival around 7:00 or 7:30 p.m. Don’t book yet.

Nashville selection prepared, not booked: campus guest hotel, January 25-28 for three nights, standard king nonsmoking, estimated tax-inclusive total $656.40, with arrival noted for approximately 7:00-7:30 p.m. The free-cancellation deadline is Friday, January 23 at 6:00 p.m. local time. I’ll also flag the need to verify the final total, room type, mandatory fees, deposit, and late-arrival guarantee.
Now Raleigh. The forum hotel is $229 nightly and the nearby business hotel is $176. Both are three-night quotes before tax.

For three nights, the forum hotel totals $776.31 including the displayed taxes. The nearby business hotel totals $596.64 including tax, a difference of $179.67. The business hotel is about a nine-minute walk from the forum venue; the forum hotel is in the same complex as the sessions.
The cheaper one says it can’t promise luggage storage after checkout. My breakfast ends at 10:30 Saturday, checkout is noon, and the flight isn’t until 6:10.

That is the main weakness of the business hotel. You could return after breakfast and check out by noon, but without storage you would need to keep the bag with you, pay for an external storage service, or leave for the airport much earlier than necessary. The forum hotel has confirmed that its bell desk will hold luggage after checkout at no charge until you collect it around 3:30 p.m.
Could a late checkout make the business hotel work?

Possibly, but its standard checkout is 11:00 a.m., and late checkout is only assigned on the morning of departure. Even a 1:00 p.m. extension would still leave several hours before the airport trip. An external luggage service plus two short car rides would likely add $35-$50 and more coordination, so it would reduce but not erase the $179.67 savings.
And the cancellation terms for those two?

The forum hotel can be cancelled without charge until 6:00 p.m. local time on Monday, January 26. The business hotel’s quoted rate is cancellable until 6:00 p.m. on Sunday, January 25. Each charges one night plus tax after its deadline. The forum hotel therefore has the later deadline as well as confirmed Saturday bag storage.
I think the forum hotel is worth it for this schedule. Select it, standard king and nonsmoking. What does the whole six-night lodging plan total?

Selected for preparation: the Raleigh forum hotel, January 28-31 for three nights, standard king nonsmoking, at an estimated $776.31 including tax. Combined with the Nashville campus guest hotel at $656.40, the six-night lodging total is $1,432.71 including displayed taxes. No hotel has been booked.
Please give me the booking details and the ground-transportation outline in one final record. Include what still has to be confirmed.

Prepared lodging record, not booked: Nashville campus guest hotel, check in Sunday, January 25 and check out Wednesday, January 28, three nights, standard king nonsmoking, late arrival approximately 7:00-7:30 p.m., estimated tax-inclusive total $656.40. Free cancellation ends Friday, January 23 at 6:00 p.m. local time. Plan on a car from BNA to the hotel Sunday, a round-trip car for Monday’s downtown dinner, and walking to Tuesday’s campus meetings. Raleigh forum hotel, check in Wednesday, January 28 and check out Saturday, January 31, three nights, standard king nonsmoking, estimated tax-inclusive total $776.31. Free cancellation ends Monday, January 26 at 6:00 p.m. local time. Walk to forum events, leave luggage with the bell desk after Saturday checkout, retrieve it around 3:30 p.m., and take a car to RDU for the 6:10 p.m. flight. Combined lodging is estimated at $1,432.71 including displayed taxes; estimated Nashville cars are about $66, while Raleigh should require the airport transfers plus any off-site event transportation. Before booking, verify live availability, exact tax-inclusive totals, room descriptions, cancellation language and time zones, mandatory fees, incidental deposits, payment timing, late-arrival protection in Nashville, and complimentary post-checkout luggage storage in Raleigh. The Monday dinner address also remains necessary to confirm the Nashville car plan.
